prompt: Write 10 distinct short extracts of Larkmere Mutual's official guidance, procedures or policy wording about: cracks appearing in the walls. Two to four sentences each, in the society's own formal voice. Use type "fact". Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"If cracks appear in external or internal walls, members should report them to Larkmere Mutual without delay and take photographs showing their location and extent. Small cracks caused by minor settlement may be monitored, but any widening, diagonal or stepped cracking, or cracking that appears suddenly should be assessed promptly by a suitable professional. We may ask for further evidence before deciding whether the damage is covered."},{"type":"fact","content":"Cracks that are consistent with subsidence, heave or landslip must be notified as soon as they are discovered. Members should avoid carrying out repairs, making alterations or removing nearby trees until Larkmere Mutual has reviewed the circumstances, as this may affect our ability to investigate the cause. We may arrange a survey or request a report from an approved engineer."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where cracks are reported, our first step is to consider whether the damage is cosmetic or whether it may indicate movement affecting the structure. Cracks wider than hairline, particularly those around doors, windows, ceilings or extensions, may require urgent inspection. If there is any sign of unsafe movement, the member should not use the affected area until it has been checked."},{"type":"fact","content":"Larkmere Mutual does not expect members to undertake invasive investigation of cracks themselves. Any opening up of walls, floors or finishes should only be carried out with our agreement, unless immediate action is required to make the home safe. We may decline cover for unnecessary work completed before we have had a reasonable opportunity to inspect the damage."},{"type":"fact","content":"Cracking caused by building works, poor workmanship or gradual wear and tear is not covered under the buildings section of the policy. However, if the cracking is accompanied by a one-off insured event, such as storm damage or impact, the claim will be considered in line with the policy wording. Members should provide dates, details of any works and any relevant contractor information."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where cracks are linked to an escape of water, members must stop the leak if it is safe to do so and notify us promptly. We may cover resulting damage to walls, plaster and decoration, subject to the terms, limits and exclusions of the policy. Ongoing dampness or repeated seepage will be treated differently from sudden and accidental damage."},{"type":"fact","content":"If cracks are found in boundary walls, retaining walls or outbuildings, the member should report them and describe any nearby ground movement, drainage issues or tree roots. These features can help establish whether the damage is related to an insured peril or to gradual causes. We may ask for ownership details and evidence of maintenance."},{"type":"fact","content":"In assessing claims involving cracks, we may take account of prior history, previous repairs and any earlier reports of movement. The presence of existing cracking does not automatically mean a claim is refused, but pre-existing damage may limit what is payable. Members should keep records of earlier inspections, quotations and correspondence where available."},{"type":"fact","content":"If cracking is worsening after severe weather, the member should tell Larkmere Mutual whether the property has been affected by high winds, heavy rain or prolonged rainfall. We may compare the timing of the damage with local weather information from the Met Office and with the visible pattern of cracking. This helps us decide whether the damage is consistent with an insured event."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where a claim for cracking is accepted, we will normally pay for reasonable remedial works necessary to return the damaged part of the building to its previous condition. We do not automatically pay for improvements, cosmetic upgrading or work to undamaged areas unless this is required to complete the repairs. Any temporary support or emergency make-safe measures must be agreed with us where practicable."}]}
